sources.name: BleepingComputer
sources.title: Hackers exploit GL.iNet cloud flaw to infect routers, KVM devices

sources.name: Hacker News
sources.title: GL.iNet Security Notice 2026-11-20

stories.headline: GL.iNet cloud flaw let attackers plant malware on routers and KVMs
stories.dek: The company has patched its remote management service and shipped security firmware, but already infected devices need checking and updating.
stories.body:
GL.iNet has confirmed that an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in its cloud remote management service to access customers' routers and KVM devices and install malicious software. In a security notice dated November 20, the company says it fixed the cloud flaw and blocked the access used, so devices can no longer be newly infected that way. The fix does not clean devices that were already compromised.

GL.iNet tells owners to look for a running process containing the exact text crond -i /tmp/.log, its main indicator of compromise. On routers that means LuCI's process list or running ps | grep tmp over SSH. On KVMs, owners run ps -aux | grep tmp in the device terminal (ps -a on the RMQ1). Everyone should install the latest stable security firmware for their exact model, even if the check comes back clean. The company says that firmware removes the identified malware and settings can be kept. Owners of infected KVMs should also check the computers they control.

The official check may miss infections. GL.iNet acknowledges additional indicators have surfaced and points to a community-built scanner, while disclaiming responsibility for it. According to BleepingComputer, the tool's developers warn some devices may need firmware reinstalled without keeping settings, since malicious files in configuration directories could survive a normal upgrade. They also advise preserving evidence and rotating exposed credentials.

BleepingComputer examined a malicious ni.sh script tailored to GL.iNet hardware. It downloads payloads named gl-helper and gb, persists through startup scripts and scheduled tasks, disguises itself as the crond process and swaps netstat for a script that hides connections to the attacker's server. It can also install SSH keys and fetch remote commands. Chinese-language comments suggest a Chinese-speaking author. Researchers at RemoteToHome Consulting say 152 of 183 routers they own or manage showed suspicious activity, including 24 with root-level reverse shells, though some older backdoors may be unrelated.

Much remains unclear. GL.iNet has not said how the flaw was exploited, how many customers were hit or whether data was stolen. Some recovered files carry December 2025 timestamps, but any link to this attack is unconfirmed. The company says it will email affected customers at their cloud account addresses.
key_points: Attackers abused GL.iNet's cloud remote management to install malware
Cloud flaw fixed; stable security firmware released for listed models
Indicator of compromise: process named crond -i /tmp/.log
Researchers found suspicious activity on 152 of 183 routers they checked
stories.why_it_matters: If a GL.iNet router or KVM sits on your network, check it and update the firmware now. An infected KVM may also expose the computer it controls.

sources.name: TechRadar
sources.title: Google claims it has seen the first fully autonomous cyberattack — and says a 'significant threshold' has been crossed in terms of cybersecurity

stories.headline: Google says AI agents now run cyberattacks on their own
stories.dek: Google's threat team found an exposed server running exploit_agent, software that reads patches, writes exploits and launches them without human help.
stories.body:
Cybercriminals have moved from chatbot helpers to software that finds, builds and runs exploits autonomously, according to Google, as reported by TechRadar. The Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant call the shift a "significant threshold," warning that machine-speed intrusions pose a new challenge for defenders.

Investigators found an unsecured staging server hosting a system called exploit_agent, linked to several cloud and local language models. It compares code before and after patches, spots flaw-related changes, writes working exploits and launches them. Scripts then mapped networks, guessed passwords and planted webshells. Victims skewed toward French media, entertainment and education sites, while config comments were in Russian.

Google says these frameworks currently "trade stealth for velocity" but expects more stealth and less human involvement ahead. It counted 11 zero-day exploits per month in 2026, up from at least 8 in 2025.
key_points: Google and Mandiant found an exposed server running exploit_agent, which turns patch diffs into working exploits automatically.
Google confirmed open source frameworks CAIRN and PentAGI were used against live targets.
Zero-day exploits rose to 11 per month in 2026, peaking at 22 in August, according to Google.

sources.name: The Hacker News
sources.title: OpenRouter Drops 3 Providers After Researchers Catch Months of Prompt Theft at AI Hosting Firms

stories.headline: OpenRouter drops three AI providers after months of prompt theft
stories.dek: Dragos canary research found attackers copying requests inside three inference hosts, including prompts flagged Zero Data Retention, while the providers never noticed.
stories.body:
OpenRouter has removed three inference providers from its platform after Dragos researchers found attackers had been stealing data from inside them for months, The Hacker News reports. The gateway also pulled 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention eligibility and notified potentially affected customers. It says its own systems were not breached.

Dragos seeded about two million prompts with unique links and credentials between July and November. The earliest breach began in mid-July, and none of the providers knew until told. In the largest case, an attacker copied every request in several late-October windows and used planted AWS keys within hours, generating tens of thousands of API calls.

Phala and Together AI have disclosed related incidents. "A privacy flag doesn't help when the attacker is already inside," wrote HD Moore, Dragos chief research officer.
key_points: OpenRouter removed three providers and 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention eligibility.
Dragos canary tests covered about two million prompts; some stolen requests were marked Zero Data Retention.
Neither Dragos nor OpenRouter has named the three providers or confirmed they are the same.

sources.name: Tom's Hardware
sources.title: TSMC reportedly pauses shipments to Chinese designers after U.S. export rules flag decade-old 16nm and 14nm nodes

stories.headline: TSMC reportedly holds shipments as US rule pulls in 16nm chips
stories.dek: A new BIS rule tells fabs to treat 16nm and 14nm chips as export-controlled AI parts, hitting phone, TV and car chips.
stories.body:
TSMC has put several shipments to Chinese and non-Chinese chip designers on hold while it reviews compliance with new US export rules, Nikkei Asia reports, according to Tom's Hardware. The Bureau of Industry and Security's interim final rule requires foundries and packaging firms to assume chips on 16nm, 14nm or newer nodes are export-controlled advanced computing chips.

The rule says fabs cannot assume a chip is not for high-performance computing just because it has fewer than 30 billion transistors and no HBM. To avoid extra scrutiny, designers must get documentation certifying the chip's Total Processing Performance or performance density. Those decade-old nodes appear in smartphones, TVs and cars.

The rule also blocks Chinese AI firms from leasing compute abroad to reach chips like Nvidia Blackwell. It adds license requirements for advanced AI chips shipped to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Brazil and Thailand, which it calls transshipment points.
key_points: Nikkei Asia reports TSMC paused some shipments to Chinese and non-Chinese designers pending compliance reviews.
The BIS rule treats chips on 16nm, 14nm or newer nodes as export-controlled unless performance is certified.
Advanced AI chip exports to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Brazil and Thailand now need licenses.

sources.name: Linuxiac
sources.title: LLVM completes eight-year relicensing to Apache 2.0 with LLVM Exceptions

stories.headline: LLVM wraps up its eight-year move to Apache 2.0 licensing
stories.dek: More than 99.5 percent of code ever contributed is now relicensed, removed or too small to copyright, so maintainers are closing the effort.
stories.body:
The LLVM Project has declared its relicensing effort complete, eight years after it began in 2018, Linuxiac reports. More than 99.5 percent of all lines of code ever contributed are now under Apache 2.0 with LLVM Exceptions, removed from the codebase, or too small to qualify for copyright. The figure covers historical contributions, not just code in the current repository.

The change replaces the original University of Illinois/NCSA license and the MIT license used by some runtime libraries. New contributions have used Apache 2.0 with LLVM Exceptions since January 19, 2019. Older code needed permission from its authors: more than 1,300 individuals and about 100 companies signed on.

Contributors who never signed can ask LLVM to tag their code with the right SPDX identifier. LICENSE files will be updated after the LLVM 24 branch, expected in early January 2027, and will ship in LLVM 25.
key_points: Over 99.5 percent of all code ever contributed to LLVM is now Apache 2.0 with LLVM Exceptions, removed, or too small to copyright.
More than 1,300 individuals and about 100 organizations agreed to relicense their past contributions.
Updated LICENSE files will appear in LLVM 25, after the LLVM 24 branch expected in early January 2027.

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: Unreal Engine 6 to jettison key scripting feature earlier than planned in favor of AI coding

stories.headline: Unreal Engine 6 drops Blueprints, bets on Verse and AI
stories.dek: Epic reverses a June plan to keep Blueprints in UE6, saying AI will help convert UE5 projects, PC Gamer reports.
stories.body:
Unreal Engine 6 will ship without Blueprints, the engine's long-standard visual scripting system, PC Gamer reports. In a November 19 post on the Unreal Engine website, Epic executive vice president of development Marcus Wassmer said UE6, including Early Access, won't include Blueprints or the Actor Gameplay Framework. Gameplay will instead be built in Verse on the new Scene Graph framework.

In June, Epic said Blueprints and Actors would coexist in UE6 so projects could upgrade incrementally. Wassmer now says AI should massively help convert UE5 projects, if not automate the process, letting UE6 ship on time or sooner. He cited falling AI costs and an AI-assisted conversion of Fortnite's Blueprint library to Verse. Blueprints remain in UE5.

Former Valve developer Chet Faliszek argues the change removes a key middle ground for designers and artists. Eric Berger, co-developer of Queen's Domain, told PC Gamer that Unreal's AI pivot is pushing his studio to switch engines.
key_points: UE6, including Early Access, will not include Blueprints or the Actor Gameplay Framework; gameplay moves to Verse and Scene Graph.
Epic had said in June that Blueprints would coexist in UE6, but now expects AI to largely handle UE5-to-UE6 conversion.
Queen's Domain developer Freshly Baked Games plans to switch engines over Unreal's AI pivot, according to PC Gamer.
